title: Unkawa Neck / Unqua Creek
summary: Unkawa was a neck-place name on the Babylon and Oyster Bay town boundary, connected with the later Unqua stream name.
history_content: The name belongs to the south-shore boundary landscape between modern Babylon and Oyster Bay town contexts. Unqua names a trout stream associated with the Floyd-Jones estate and appears to derive from the Unkawa neck through which it flows.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Unkawa and Unkaway. The name is interpreted as the furthermost, describing a neck understood as the furthermost neck of either town.

Unqua is treated as a related stream form of Unkawa. The underlying meaning follows Unkawa as the furthermost.

Why Place Names Matter

“All we know, for example, is that the Southampton settlers named their community after a town in England, whereas Smithtown and Gardiners Island reflect the egos of two prominent colonial settlers. In Patchogue and Ronkonkoma, however, the Indian names survived.”

— John A. Strong, William Wallace Tooker (2003), Long Island Historical Journal, Vol. 16, Nos. 1–2, p. 149
preservation_content: Unkawa preserves a boundary-place name whose later memory survives around Unqua Creek, Unqua Road, and Massapequa-area local names.
whereintheworld_content: Blue/general approximate marker near the Unqua Creek / East Massapequa and Amityville boundary landscape. This point is for orientation only and is not an exact historic neck, estate, or stream coordinate.
